references.text: Reiterates the principle of one law for both Israelites and foreigners living among them, especially regarding unintentional sins.
The same law shall apply to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you - a fundamental principle of equality before the law.
One law shall apply to you, to the foreigner as well as to the native-born, emphasizing equality in the legal system.
The same regulation applies to both the foreigner and the native-born concerning the celebration of Passover.
Both foreigners and native-born are subject to the same rules for the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The foreigner shall be as a native-born, and you shall love him as yourself - expanding on the principle of equality.
In Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek - New Testament fulfillment of the principle of equality before God.
Those who were foreigners to the covenants are now brought near by the blood of Christ - Gentiles fully included.
Neither Greek nor Jew, circumcised nor uncircumcised - all are one in Christ, fulfilling the principle of one law for all.
